email.body1:
Aarason, saw Stampli closed its $61M Series D led by Blackstone and launched Deep Finance.

A new product and fresh capital usually mean more in-market accounts than the team can cover before reps ramp on the message, and that is where pipeline cools. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for your region off hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes to walk you through it?
email.subject2: meetings to hit your region's number
email.body2:
Aarason, quick follow-up for your Stampli region.

Post-raise, expectations on pipeline usually climb faster than headcount can. Most leaders don't know exactly how many meetings each rep needs to book to hit the new number, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your region needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Aarason, last bit of proof for your Stampli team.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your reply rate likely compares to peer fintech teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Aarason, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling regional pipeline without adding reps isn't a priority right after the raise, no problem at all. The fundraise-to-scale stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your regional motion? I'll tailor it to Stampli either way.
